contracts.commit_point: Registration-time commit: the filtered tool list is bound into create_agent in LangChainRootCauseAgent.analyze (root_cause.py lines 155-167), fixing the agent's invocable tool set; the guarded effect itself — an MCP tool invocation dispatched over HTTP to the 'kubernetes' server — commits during agent.ainvoke tool execution (root_cause.py lines 170-172). Both commit points fall in the same effect stratum, so a single contract is emitted.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Name-based tool allowlist: the module-level frozenset ALLOWED_MCP_TOOL_NAMES (root_cause.py line 21) is enforced inside load_read_only_mcp_tools, which returns only loaded tools whose name attribute is in the allowlist (root_cause.py lines 99-100); LangChainRootCauseAgent.analyze loads exactly this filtered list and registers it with create_agent (root_cause.py lines 156-160).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Any kubernetes MCP tool whose name is not in ALLOWED_MCP_TOOL_NAMES {kubectl_get, kubectl_describe, kubectl_logs} — in particular any mutating kubectl operation — being registered into the agent built by create_agent or being invoked by the LLM agent during agent.ainvoke against the cluster.
pending_binding_information: Server-side semantics of the 'kubernetes' MCP server (default http://localhost:3001/mcp): whether kubectl_get/kubectl_describe/kubectl_logs are genuinely read-only and whether the server exposes additional tools beyond the three allowlisted names is not shown in the supplied source.

Concrete dataflow from RootCauseAnalysisHandler/KubernetesEventCollector to LangChainRootCauseAgent.analyze (the my_agent_app.collector module is not supplied); main.py lines 32-41 show only construction and wiring of the agent into the FastAPI lifespan pipeline.
Whether langchain's create_agent/ainvoke guarantees that the agent cannot invoke tools outside the registered list at runtime (framework behavior and version not shown in the supplied source).
contracts.protected_operation: The LLM root-cause agent's read-only diagnostic investigation of Kubernetes warning events via the allowlisted MCP tools (kubectl_get, kubectl_describe, kubectl_logs) during LangChainRootCauseAgent.analyze and its agent.ainvoke run.
contracts.protected_resource: The Kubernetes cluster reachable through the 'kubernetes' MCP server at settings.mcp_server_url (default http://localhost:3001/mcp, overridable via the MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable).
contracts.protection_obligation: MCP tools loaded from the 'kubernetes' MCP server must be filtered to the read-only allowlist ALLOWED_MCP_TOOL_NAMES = {kubectl_get, kubectl_describe, kubectl_logs} by load_read_only_mcp_tools before the resulting tool list is registered with create_agent in LangChainRootCauseAgent.analyze, so that the LLM agent can invoke only allowlisted read-only kubectl operations and can never register or invoke any mutating or otherwise non-allowlisted tool against the cluster. (Merges the two reviewer phrasings, which describe the same single obligation.)
scope_limits: Applies only to tools loaded from the single 'kubernetes' MCP server configured in load_read_only_mcp_tools (root_cause.py lines 90-98); no other MCP servers, direct kubectl execution, or alternative Kubernetes API access paths are covered by this guard.

The guard filters tools solely by name (getattr(tool, 'name', '') in ALLOWED_MCP_TOOL_NAMES, root_cause.py line 100); it does not constrain tool arguments, namespaces, resource selectors, or output handling for the allowlisted read-only tools.

Enforcement occurs once at tool load/registration time; per-invocation re-validation and any framework guarantee that the agent can only dispatch registered tools are not established by the supplied source.

ROOT_CAUSE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (root_cause.py lines 103-109) is advisory prompt-level guidance ('Investigue apenas com as ferramentas de leitura fornecidas'); the enforceable mechanism for this obligation is the name allowlist, not the prompt.
ModelCallLimitMiddleware (root_cause.py lines 162-166) bounds LLM call volume and is a separate mechanism outside this allowlist obligation.
Server-side authorization or read-only enforcement inside the 'kubernetes' MCP server itself is outside the supplied source and outside this contract's declared mechanism.
